finding_the_preservation_asset_had_partl.why_it_did_not_break_the_precondition: Recipe items 5 and 6 read the ref out of the BUNDLE, not out of a checkout, and both passed. The bundle was and is a self-sufficient recovery source. The tag's absence from every working repository is a loss of convenience and of a second, independent copy -- not a loss of recoverability.
finding_the_preservation_asset_had_partl.what_i_did_about_it: Re-created refs/tags/freeze/k0-aa67c426 at aa67c426afaa9b6ca91c9996637a6bade950da9a in /pscratch/sd/j/josephrb/MINERvA-OmniFold (local-only, not pushed, matching the original's deliberate non-pushed status). It is not created in the deploy tree, because the 2026-08-26 receipt's detectability recipe asserts that tree's ref set is 'exactly ten rows and no others' and adding an eleventh row for a historical pin would falsify a passing check for no gain.
finding_the_preservation_asset_had_partl.the_generalisation_this_lane_acted_on: A single-copy, unpushed, working-checkout-resident ref is preservation only for as long as that checkout exists, and nothing in the receipt made its disappearance detectable. The new freeze ref for 7ac0edec is therefore created in TWO repositories, and its bundle is asserted to contain it, so the same decay is detectable next time.
